ecological_question: Do individual bats show repeatable cross-session differences in their vertical flight response to modeled vertical wind?

training_weighting.self: equal session coefficient mean from the same individual excluding the target session
training_weighting.population: equal-individual coefficient mean from all other individuals

primary.endpoint: absolute slope error improvement = |target slope - population-predicted slope| - |target slope - self-predicted slope|
primary.positive_meaning: the individual's own other sessions predict its uplift-response slope better than other bats do

secondary.target_fix_mse_improvement: MSE(population regression on target fixes) - MSE(self regression on the same target fixes)

slope_identity_permutation.statistic: within-individual sum of squared deviations of session slopes from individual means
slope_identity_permutation.tail: smaller observed within-individual variation indicates repeatability

agl_context.semantics: height above ground level from 30 m ASTER DEM, m
agl_context.role: descriptive and later moderation analysis; cannot replace the primary uplift reaction norm

claim_boundary: positive repeatability supports stable individual reaction norms to modeled vertical wind under this dataset
does not establish genetic personality, learning, optimality, or causal preference
does not establish foraging because no validated foraging-state label is present
mechanism analysis cannot alter the previously obtained place-by-height self-transfer result
